title: Teen-age Guru's Secret 'Divine Light' (Fifth Estate, September 14, 1973)
author: Len Schafer, interviewing an initiate identified as 'Amy'
edition_cited: Fifth Estate (Detroit), September 14, 1973, pp. 6-7, as reproduced at ex-premie.org/pages/fifthestate4.htm
tradition: Divine Light Mission (Prem Rawat, 'Knowledge'); ex-initiate informant
locator_hints: Article 'Teen-age Guru's Secret Divine Light', interview with Amy: paragraph on Divine Light (pressure on the outer areas of the eyes; 'head is flooded with light'); the retinal-damage warning; closing answer on feeling no bliss
Also: six hours with a mahatma; secrecy threat; the 'braggan' board for the sound technique
summary: An early public disclosure of the four Divine Light Mission techniques, given to an underground paper by a recent initiate. For the light technique she says only that one presses on the eyes: because the retina responds to pressure as well as to light, pressure on the outer areas fires the nerve cells and gives 'the sensation that your head is flooded with light'. She treats it as physiology, adds that most doctors would warn that pressing to get this light could damage the retina, and says the hours of talk beforehand make the suggestible receptive. Asked whether she felt bliss afterwards she says no. The piece also describes the sound, breath and tongue techniques and the roughly six-hour initiation. No detail of finger placement or duration, and no claim that the light persists without pressure.
why_relevant: Dated 1973 testimony that the DLM light was produced by eye pressure, with the practitioner's own deflationary reading and an explicit safety warning; evidence on the stimulus-bound side.

date_evidence.basis: Magazine issue date and page numbers as printed on the reproduction page ('Fifth Estate Magazine Article - September 14, 1973', pp. 6-7); the magazine itself was not seen, and the web page carries no posting date.

author_basis: Bylined journalist (Len Schafer) in Fifth Estate, a Detroit periodical published since 1965; the informant is pseudonymous
notes: Safety: eye pressure. Reader extract of a web reproduction of a magazine article; anchors only from the quoted phrases. Likely stimulus_bound_only on its own evidence: keep as counter-testimony to the lineage's claims.
